claims.claim: A STRIDE/DREAD threat model comparing seven major MCP clients rated tool poisoning, coercive instructions embedded in tool metadata, the most prevalent and impactful client-side vulnerability.
claims.reason: Excerpt states tool poisoning (malicious instructions in tool metadata) is the most prevalent and impactful client-side vulnerability, with a systematic comparison of seven major MCP clients.

claims.claim: The seven-client comparison traced the tool-poisoning weakness to insufficient static validation and insufficient parameter visibility in most tested clients.
claims.reason: Excerpt attributes the security issues in most tested clients to insufficient static validation and parameter visibility.

claims.claim: The weakness is a protocol-level default rather than one product's bug: the reference implementation ships without guard rails, so every conforming client inherits the exposure.
claims.reason: Excerpt confirms the reference implementation ships without guard rails and developers lack a security baseline, supporting the protocol-default framing.
